command: ls -la documents output; for f in documents/*; do echo "=== $f"; parse-doc "$f" | wc -c; done

cd /workspace; for f in documents/*.docx; do echo "== $f"; unzip -l "$f" | awk "{print \$4}"; unzip -p "$f" word/document.xml | grep -o "<w:\(ins\|del\|vanish\|commentReference\)[^>]*>" | sort | uniq -c | head; for p in word/header1.xml word/footer1.xml word/footer2.xml word/header2.xml word/comments.xml word/footnotes.xml; do unzip -p "$f" $p 2>/dev/null | sed -e "s/<[^>]*>//g" | head -c 500; echo; done; done; ls skills/docx/scripts; python3 -c "import docx;print(docx.__version__)"

mkdir -p /workspace/work && cat > /workspace/work/items.py <<"PYEOF"
ITEMS = [
dict(id="D-1", area="A. Structure and Interim Status",
 title="Supersession of the Term Sheet; integration clause; Engagement Letter becomes the baseline for the Definitive Agreement",
 ref="TS §§16, 17, 18 / EL §1, §14, §16.3",
 ts="TS §16: the binding engagement letter for the interim period “shall be consistent with the terms of this Term Sheet”; the Definitive Agreement “shall incorporate the terms set forth in this Term Sheet.” TS §17: §8 (Exclusivity), §14 (Confidentiality) and §15 (Governing Law/Dispute Resolution) are binding and “shall remain in effect regardless of whether the Definitive Agreement is executed.”",
 el="EL §1: “supersedes the Term Sheet in its entirety”; EL controls in any conflict; undefined capitalized terms take Term Sheet meanings. EL §16.3: entire agreement superseding all prior agreements “including without limitation the Term Sheet.” EL §14: the Definitive Agreement “shall incorporate the terms set forth in this Engagement Letter.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "This is the mechanism that makes every other deviation in this report operative. Once countersigned, the Engagement Letter (i) extinguishes the Term Sheet, including the three provisions that are binding today (TS §§8, 14 and 15); (ii) replaces the Term Sheet as the reference document for the Definitive Agreement (EL §14 now says the Definitive Agreement will incorporate the terms of the Engagement Letter, not the Term Sheet); and (iii) through the integration clause in EL §16.3, eliminates any argument that the Term Sheet bargain (the field-of-use compromise, the Joint IP sublicensing guardrail, the MFN/non-compete package) informs interpretation.",
  "Practical consequence: if Stellarion signs this letter as drafted, Helix will open the Definitive Agreement negotiation from the Engagement Letter positions (broader field, free Joint IP licensing, lower minimum royalty, uncapped indemnity, and so on), and Stellarion would have to re-trade terms it already won in February.",
  "Collateral effects: (a) the binding Term Sheet confidentiality covenant (TS §14) covers all information exchanged “in connection with the transactions contemplated” since discussions began in Q4 2024; the Engagement Letter covenant covers information “received in connection with this Agreement” (EL §10.1), leaving a gap for pre-letter disclosures once TS §14 is superseded; (b) importing Term Sheet definitions is internally inconsistent with superseding the Term Sheet “in its entirety” and with the Engagement Letter’s own, different definitions (e.g., “Effective Date”).",
  "Leverage note: the Term Sheet’s “consistent with” covenant (TS §16) is not one of the listed Binding Provisions, so Stellarion’s leverage is primarily commercial rather than a breach claim. The cleanest leverage is that Stellarion has not signed: the version we received is unsigned by either party (see D-60), and nothing in it binds Stellarion until countersignature.",
 ],
 position="Replace the supersession language with a statement that the Engagement Letter implements the Term Sheet for the interim period; provide that the Term Sheet Binding Provisions remain in effect except to the extent expressly restated; provide that the Definitive Agreement “shall incorporate the terms set forth in the Term Sheet, as supplemented by this Engagement Letter”; and expressly extend the confidentiality covenant to all information disclosed since the start of discussions in Q4 2024."),

dict(id="D-2", area="A. Structure and Interim Status",
 title="Present, binding license grant effective on signing of the Engagement Letter; “Effective Date” moved from Definitive Agreement execution to Engagement Letter countersignature",
 ref="TS §2, §3.1, §4.1 / EL §3 (“Effective Date”), §4.1, §4.2, §5.1",
 ts="TS §2: Stellarion “proposes to grant” the license “[s]ubject to the terms and conditions of the Definitive Agreement.” TS §3.1: the Effective Date “shall be defined as the date of execution of the Definitive Agreement.” Upfront fee payable on execution of the Definitive Agreement (TS §4.1).",
 el="EL §4.1: Stellarion “hereby grants” the license now. EL §3: “Effective Date” is the date of last countersignature of the Engagement Letter. The upfront fee is still payable only after execution of the Definitive Agreement (EL §5.1). License Term, Project Meridian period, Exclusivity Period and escrow deposit deadline all run from the Engagement Letter Effective Date.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The Term Sheet contemplated that the interim engagement letter would govern the parties’ obligations pending the Definitive Agreement, not that it would itself convey the license. As drafted, Helix receives an immediate, binding, worldwide license to Stellarion’s crown-jewel technology on countersignature, while the $12.5 million upfront fee is not payable until a Definitive Agreement that may never be signed. Combined with the open-ended interim term in EL §14 (D-3), Helix could hold a live license indefinitely without paying any upfront consideration, paying only running royalties and, from Year 2, a reduced minimum royalty.",
  "Moving the Effective Date to the Engagement Letter date also shifts every clock in the deal: the five-year Initial Term, the 24-month Project Meridian window, the Exclusivity Period and the 30-day escrow deposit deadline (EL §12) all start before any money changes hands, and a source code deposit is triggered before Stellarion has been paid (D-47).",
  "This structural change is not one of the three items the GC flagged but, in our view, belongs in the dealbreaker category because it converts an interim letter into the operative license on Helix-favorable terms.",
 ],
 position="Reject. The Engagement Letter should contain no present license grant. Either (a) delete the grant in EL §4.1 and state that the license “shall be granted under, and effective upon execution of, the Definitive Agreement, and conditioned upon Stellarion’s receipt of the first installment of the Upfront License Fee”; or (b) if Helix needs pre-closing integration access, grant a narrow evaluation license (object code, internal non-production use only, within the Licensed Field, terminable on notice). Restore “Effective Date” to mean the date of execution of the Definitive Agreement (TS §3.1)."),

dict(id="D-3", area="A. Structure and Interim Status",
 title="Target date for the Definitive Agreement moved to May 30, 2025; Engagement Letter continues indefinitely if no Definitive Agreement is signed",
 ref="TS §16 / EL §14",
 ts="Negotiate in good faith to execute the Definitive Agreement on or before May 15, 2025 (the Target Closing Date).",
 el="Good faith and commercially reasonable efforts to execute by May 30, 2025; if not executed by then, the Engagement Letter “shall continue in full force and effect until terminated by either Party upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The 15-day slip is modest in itself, and the added “commercially reasonable efforts” standard is a slight improvement over good faith alone. The real issue is the evergreen tail: because the Engagement Letter grants a present license (D-2) at reduced economics, an indefinite interim period lets Helix operate under Engagement Letter terms without ever closing, which gives Helix an incentive to slow-walk the Definitive Agreement.",
  "The 60-day termination right is mutual and gives Stellarion an exit, and termination ends the license (EL §11.3). That right is worth keeping, but the default should be automatic expiry, not continuation.",
 ],
 position="Restore May 15, 2025 as the Target Closing Date; add an outside date (e.g., June 30, 2025) on which the Engagement Letter automatically expires unless extended in writing, with confidentiality, exclusivity and dispute resolution surviving; keep Stellarion’s right to terminate on notice at any time after the outside date."),

dict(id="D-4", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="FIELD OF USE: “predictive analytics” added; supply chain optimization exclusion and Helix covenant not to use, market or deploy in supply chain deleted [GC PRIORITY 1]",
 ref="TS §2 (Field of Use) / EL §4.1",
 ts="“The license shall be limited to data infrastructure and edge computing applications. The license expressly excludes supply chain optimization, which constitutes Stellarion’s core market. Helix shall not use, market, or deploy Stellarion EdgeAI™ in any product, service, or solution directed at supply chain optimization use cases.”",
 el="“The license granted hereunder shall be limited to use in connection with data infrastructure, edge computing, and predictive analytics applications.” No supply chain exclusion; no negative covenant.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["See Part IV.1 for the full analysis."],

dict(id="D-5", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Licensed products expanded to “products and services”; “Helix Edge Runtime” defined to include all updates, upgrades and successive versions",
 ref="TS §2 (Grant) / EL §3, §4.1",
 ts="Integration “solely into Helix Edge Runtime products and related documentation.” Helix Edge Runtime not defined.",
 el="“[S]olely for integration into Helix Edge Runtime products and services”; “Helix Edge Runtime” includes “all updates, upgrades, and successive versions thereof.”",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Adding “services” extends the license from distributed product to hosted, managed and professional-services offerings (e.g., Helix-operated analytics delivered to customers), which are harder to monitor, harder to audit for royalties and easier to direct at supply chain customers. The open-ended “successive versions” definition invites Helix to argue that a re-platformed or rebranded product family, potentially including analytics products far from the edge runtime, is still “Helix Edge Runtime.”",
  "This compounds the field-of-use expansion: the broader the product perimeter, the more weight the field restriction must bear.",
 ],
 position="Revert to “Helix Edge Runtime products and related documentation.” If Helix needs a services right, limit it to hosted delivery of Helix Edge Runtime itself, within the Licensed Field, with royalties on all associated revenue. Define Helix Edge Runtime by a product description schedule; successor versions qualify only if they remain an edge compute platform of substantially the same function; merging Helix Edge Runtime into other Helix products does not expand the license."),

dict(id="D-6", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Sublicensing of the licensed technology: consent mechanism replaced with “except as expressly set forth in this Agreement”; Affiliate use unaddressed",
 ref="TS §2 (Sublicensing) / EL §4.1, §3 (“Gross Revenue”)",
 ts="“Helix may not sublicense the licensed technology to any third party without the prior written consent of Stellarion.”",
 el="“Helix shall have no right to sublicense the rights granted hereunder except as expressly set forth in this Agreement.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Neutral / ambiguous", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "On its face the Engagement Letter is not less restrictive: nothing in it expressly permits sublicensing, and the escrow license in EL §12 expressly prohibits it. However, (i) “except as expressly set forth” is a hook Helix will try to fill in the Definitive Agreement (Affiliates, OEMs, channel partners, contractors); (ii) the royalty base counts revenue of Helix’s “Affiliates” (EL §3), implying Affiliate exploitation, although the license runs only to Helix; and (iii) the free M&A assignment right (EL §16.2; D-54) operates as a de facto transfer of the license without consent.",
  "Neither document addresses end-customer terms. The Definitive Agreement should require Helix to distribute EdgeAI only in object code, embedded in Helix Edge Runtime, under end-user terms at least as protective as a Stellarion-approved minimum (no reverse engineering, field restriction, no further sublicensing).",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet formulation (“Helix may not sublicense … without the prior written consent of Stellarion”); Affiliates may exercise rights only with Stellarion’s consent, with Helix liable for their compliance; add minimum end-user license terms."),

dict(id="D-7", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="License limited to object code; source code access only through escrow",

 el="Distribution “in object code form”; no source code access except under the escrow release conditions (EL §12).",

dict(id="D-8", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="New reservation of rights clause",
 ref="TS — / EL §4.3",

dict(id="D-9", area="B. License Grant, Field of Use and Term",
 title="Renewal: two 3-year renewal terms (maximum 11 years) instead of two 2-year terms (maximum 9 years); non-renewal notice cut from 180 to 120 days",
 ref="TS §3.2 / EL §4.2",
 ts="Two successive 2-year renewals; maximum total term 9 years; non-renewal notice at least 180 days before expiry.",
 el="Two successive 3-year renewals (maximum 11 years); non-renewal notice at least 120 days before expiry.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The renewal structure adds two years of potential license term to Stellarion’s flagship technology at economics fixed in 2025, and lengthens each lock-in increment from two to three years. Non-renewal is mutual, but the longer increments reduce Stellarion’s ability to reprice or exit, and the 120-day window gives Stellarion less time to plan a transition once Helix’s intentions are known.",
  "Offsetting point: the non-compete runs during the License Term, so a longer term extends Helix’s restriction. With the shorter post-term tail (D-29) and lower minimum royalty (D-15), however, the longer term is not a good trade for Stellarion.",
 ],
 position="Restore two successive two-year renewal periods (maximum nine years) and the 180-day non-renewal notice."),

dict(id="D-10", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Upfront fee installments restructured from $7.5M / $5.0M to two equal $6.25M installments",
 ref="TS §4.1 / EL §5.1",
 ts="$12,500,000 total: $7,500,000 due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement; $5,000,000 due on the six-month anniversary.",
 el="$12,500,000 total: $6,250,000 within 10 business days following execution of the Definitive Agreement; $6,250,000 on the six-month anniversary.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The headline number is unchanged, which makes this easy to miss on a skim. But $1,250,000 moves from the signing installment to the six-month installment, increasing Stellarion’s credit exposure to Helix on the deferred tranche from $5.0 million to $6.25 million (25% more) and deferring cash Stellarion expected at closing. Illustratively, at an 8% annual cost of capital the time-value cost of the shift alone is about $48,000, before credit risk and the extra 10-business-day delay on the first installment (D-11).",
  "Stellarion’s protection on the deferred tranche is also weak: no acceleration on Helix termination, assignment or change of control, and no late-payment interest outside the audit context (D-19).",
 ],
 position="Restore $7,500,000 on execution and $5,000,000 at six months. Add acceleration of the second installment on any termination by Helix (other than for Stellarion’s uncured breach), any termination by Stellarion for Helix breach or insolvency, and any assignment by Helix under the M&A exception."),

dict(id="D-11", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="First installment payable “within ten (10) business days following” execution rather than “upon execution”; wire instruction deadline added",
 ref="TS §4.1(a) / EL §5.1(a) and final paragraph",
 ts="First installment due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement; payment by wire to an account designated by Stellarion in writing.",
 el="First installment due within 10 business days after execution; Stellarion must provide wire instructions at least 5 business days before the payment date.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Up to two additional weeks of delay on $6.25 million (or $7.5 million once restored), during which Helix would already hold the license. The wire instruction requirement is operationally sensible but, as drafted, could be argued to be a condition to Helix’s payment obligation."],
 position="Payment due upon execution of the Definitive Agreement. Stellarion delivers wire instructions at signing; any delay in instructions extends the due date only day-for-day."),

dict(id="D-12", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Royalty base changed from Net Revenue (received, less returns, allowances, trade discounts, sales taxes) to Gross Revenue (GAAP-recognized revenue of Helix and its Affiliates, before any deductions)",
 ref="TS §4.2 / EL §3 (“Gross Revenue”), §5.2",
 ts="4.5% of Net Revenue: “gross revenue actually received by Helix … less returns, allowances, trade discounts, and sales taxes actually incurred.”",
 el="4.5% of Gross Revenue: “all revenue recognized by Helix or its Affiliates” from products and services that “incorporate or utilize” EdgeAI, under GAAP, “prior to any deductions for returns, allowances, discounts, shipping, taxes, or other adjustments.”",
 sev="Minor", favors="Stellarion", action="Accept",
 analysis=[
  "This deviation favors Stellarion: the rate is unchanged but the base is larger (no deductions), includes Affiliate revenue, covers products that merely “utilize” EdgeAI, and is measured on recognition rather than cash receipt. Illustratively, on $50 million of attributable gross revenue with 8% deductions, the Engagement Letter royalty is $2.25 million against $2.07 million under the Term Sheet (about $180,000 more per year).",
  "Cautions: (i) Helix may have intended this as a trade for other concessions (e.g., the lower minimum royalty), or it may be an error Helix will reverse once noticed; (ii) GAAP recognition for subscription offerings is ratable, which can defer royalties relative to billings; (iii) “attributable to” is undefined, so for bundled offerings Helix will argue only a fraction of the bundle price is attributable. The Definitive Agreement needs an allocation method (e.g., royalty on the full price of any SKU that includes EdgeAI functionality, or a per-unit minimum).",
  "Negotiating posture: Stellarion’s overall message is “conform to the Term Sheet,” and holding on to a Stellarion-favorable deviation slightly weakens that message. We recommend retaining Gross Revenue in the redline as a tradable item that can be conceded (reverting to Net Revenue) in exchange for restoration of the dealbreaker items.",
 ],
 position="Accept (retain) in the redline; add a bundled-revenue allocation rule and extend audit rights to Affiliates. Be prepared to revert to Term Sheet Net Revenue as a concession."),

dict(id="D-15", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Minimum Annual Royalty reduced from $3,000,000 to $2,500,000",
 ref="TS §4.3 / EL §5.3",
 ts="Minimum annual royalty of $3,000,000 from Year 2 onward, including renewal periods.",
 el="Minimum Annual Royalty of $2,500,000 from the second year of the License Term onward.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[

  "The minimum royalty is Stellarion’s main protection against Helix taking the license and under-commercializing (or shelving) EdgeAI, and it is one of the numbers the board will focus on.",
 ],

 title="Minimum royalty shortfall payable within 60 days (not 30); reconciliation date fixed at the last day of each Royalty Year",
 ref="TS §4.3 / EL §5.3",
 ts="Shortfall payable within 30 days of the annual reconciliation date (date to be set in the Definitive Agreement).",

dict(id="D-17", area="C. Financial Terms",

dict(id="D-18", area="C. Financial Terms",
 title="Audit mechanics: nationally recognized firm; on-site at Helix; 1.5% per month interest; records retained 3 years after each Royalty Year; Affiliates not covered",
 ref="TS §4.4 / EL §5.4",

 title="No general late-payment interest or remedy for late fees and royalties",

dict(id="D-20", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New Steering Committee with authority to set milestones, approve work plans, allocate resources and resolve disputes; no voting or deadlock mechanism",
 ref="TS §5.1 / EL §6.1",

dict(id="D-21", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Cost split changed from 60% Helix / 40% Stellarion to 55% Helix / 45% Stellarion",

dict(id="D-22", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="Cost overruns shared automatically pro rata; Term Sheet requirement of mutual written approval for overruns above 10% deleted",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="“Any cost overruns exceeding ten percent (10%) of the estimated budget shall require mutual written approval of both parties before such overruns are incurred.”",

 title="Rule that each party bears its own personnel costs omitted; reciprocal quarterly invoicing for “costs incurred” (shared cost pool undefined)",
 ref="TS §5.2 / EL §6.2",
 ts="Each party bears its own personnel costs (salaries, benefits, overhead); only shared costs (third-party tools, cloud infrastructure, testing services) are split; quarterly allocation per the plan.",

dict(id="D-24", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="JOINT IP SUBLICENSING: prior written consent requirement deleted; each party may “license” Joint IP without consent [GC PRIORITY 2]",

dict(id="D-25", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="“Joint IP” narrowed to IP jointly created by both parties’ personnel; Meridian IP created by one party alone falls outside joint ownership",
 ref="TS §5.3 (“Co-Developed IP”) / EL §3 (“Joint IP”), §6.3",
 ts="“All intellectual property arising from Project Meridian, including all inventions, discoveries, improvements, works of authorship, software, algorithms, and related documentation” is jointly owned.",
 el="Joint IP is IP “conceived, created, developed, or reduced to practice jointly by employees or contractors of both Parties in the course of, and arising from, Project Meridian.” No rule for IP created by one party alone.",
 sev="Material", favors="Ambiguous (likely Helix)", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "Under the Term Sheet everything arising from Project Meridian is joint; under the Engagement Letter only jointly-created IP is joint, and Meridian work product created by one party’s team alone would by default belong to the creating party. Helix is likely to perform most of the integration engineering on Helix Edge Runtime, so this gap could leave Helix as sole owner of significant Meridian deliverables, free of any sublicensing restriction at all.",
  "The narrower definition also interacts with the Background IP boundary (D-27): EdgeAI improvements Stellarion makes alone during Meridian fall outside Joint IP (good for Stellarion) but may also fall outside Stellarion Background IP if any Helix “resources” were used.",
  "A related gap exists in both documents: neither carves out improvements to, or derivatives of, a party’s Background IP from co-developed IP. Under the Term Sheet’s broad definition, improvements to EdgeAI arising from Meridian would be jointly owned. The Definitive Agreement should provide that improvements and derivatives of Stellarion Background IP (including EdgeAI) vest solely in Stellarion, and of Helix Background IP solely in Helix, with the rest of the Meridian output jointly owned.",
 ],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet scope (all IP arising from Project Meridian), subject to a carve-out that improvements, modifications and derivatives of a party’s Background IP belong to that party, with a license back for Meridian purposes only."),

dict(id="D-26", area="D. Project Meridian Co-Development",
 title="New Joint IP prosecution cooperation, vesting cooperation and equal (50/50) sharing of filing and prosecution costs",

dict(id="D-27", area="E. Background IP",
 title="“Background IP” redefined: includes IP “licensed to” a party; measured at the Engagement Letter date; independently developed IP excluded if it uses any of the other party’s Confidential Information or “resources”",
 ref="TS §6 / EL §3 (“Background IP”), §7",
 ts="All pre-existing IP of each party, and IP developed by it “prior to or independently of the co-development activities,” remains that party’s sole property.",
 el="Background IP is IP “owned by or licensed to a Party as of the Effective Date, or developed or acquired by a Party independently of this Agreement and without use of the other Party’s Confidential Information or resources.” Ownership language in §7 otherwise tracks the Term Sheet and adds “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise.”",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["(i) “Licensed to”: Background IP is the trigger for each party’s indemnity (EL §9.1), so including in-licensed IP expands Stellarion’s indemnity to third-party components in EdgeAI (open source or commercial libraries), uncapped under EL §9.2 (D-35). (ii) The “without use of … resources” test is vague; Helix could argue that EdgeAI improvements Stellarion develops using Helix-provided test environments are not Stellarion Background IP. (iii) The added “by implication, estoppel, or otherwise” language helps Stellarion and should be kept."],
 position="Define Stellarion Background IP to include EdgeAI and all improvements, modifications and derivatives of it however and whenever developed; delete “or resources”; decouple the indemnity trigger from in-licensed IP (D-37)."),

dict(id="D-28", area="E. Background IP",
 title="New royalty-free cross-license of each party’s Background IP to perform Project Meridian",
 ref="TS — / EL §7 (third paragraph)",
 ts="No Background IP license for co-development (the EdgeAI license itself is royalty-bearing and field-limited).",
 el="Each party grants the other “a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free license to use such Party’s Background IP solely to the extent necessary … to perform its obligations under Project Meridian,” ending on completion of Meridian or termination.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["A performance license is reasonable in principle, but as drafted it gives Helix a royalty-free right to use all Stellarion Background IP (including the 14 patents, 7 applications and EdgeAI trade secrets) without the field-of-use limit, without an express no-sublicense rule (it is only “non-transferable”), and without express confidentiality conditions. It is also silent on what rights Helix has in Stellarion Background IP to commercialize Meridian afterwards; Helix may argue that its right to “exploit, use, license” Joint IP (EL §6.3) carries an implied license to the EdgeAI technology needed to practice it."],
 position="Limit to internal development use for Project Meridian within the Licensed Field, non-sublicensable (other than to approved subcontractors bound by confidentiality), subject to EL §10; and state expressly that commercial exploitation of Meridian that incorporates or requires Stellarion Background IP requires, and is subject to the field, royalty and sublicensing terms of, the EdgeAI license."),

dict(id="D-29", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete post-termination period cut from 18 to 12 months",

dict(id="D-30", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",
 title="Non-compete scope narrowed: “otherwise exploit” and “in collaboration with any third party” deleted; new carve-out for third-party components that are not a “standalone” ML inference engine",
 ref="TS §7 / EL §8.1",
 ts="Helix shall not “develop, market, license, or otherwise exploit” a competing ML inference engine for edge computing, “whether independently or in collaboration with any third party”; the restriction covers “standalone or embedded ML inference engine technology that would be a functional substitute” for EdgeAI.",
 el="Helix shall not “develop, market, distribute, or license (or engage any third party to develop on its behalf)” a competing engine. New: use of third-party components that provide “ancillary analytics or data processing functions but do not constitute a standalone ML inference engine” is not a breach.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=["Three loopholes: (i) deleting “otherwise exploit” removes Helix’s own use and deployment of a competing engine (including in hosted services) and investment in, or acquisition of, a competing engine business; (ii) replacing “in collaboration with any third party” with “engage any third party to develop on its behalf” permits joint ventures, co-development, reseller and OEM arrangements in which the third party owns the competing engine; (iii) the new “standalone” carve-out inverts the Term Sheet, which expressly covered “standalone or embedded” engines. Helix could embed a third-party inference capability inside Helix Edge Runtime and argue it is an “ancillary” component that is not “standalone.”"],
 position="Restore the Term Sheet operative language (“develop, market, license, distribute, use, deploy or otherwise exploit … whether independently or in collaboration with any third party”; “standalone or embedded”). Any carve-out should be limited to third-party components that do not perform machine learning inference and are not a functional substitute for any EdgeAI function."),

dict(id="D-31", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",

dict(id="D-32", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",

dict(id="D-33", area="F. Non-Compete, Exclusivity and MFN",

dict(id="D-35", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnification carved OUT of the liability cap (uncapped), reversing the Term Sheet’s express statement that indemnity is within the cap",
 ref="TS §10, §11 / EL §9.2",
 ts="“For the avoidance of doubt, indemnification obligations under Section 10 are subject to and included within the aggregate liability cap.” Only exclusions: confidentiality breaches; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Cap does not apply to “(A) a Party’s indemnification obligations under Section 9.1,” confidentiality breaches, or willful misconduct or fraud. The consequential damages waiver also does not apply to these carve-outs.",
 sev="Dealbreaker", favors="Helix", action="Reject",
 analysis=[
  "The indemnity is mutual in form but asymmetric in substance. Stellarion contributes the core licensed technology, which Helix will distribute worldwide across roughly 3,400 enterprise customers, so Stellarion’s IP indemnity is the obligation most likely to be called. Removing it from the cap and from the consequential damages waiver exposes Stellarion to unlimited liability, including customers’ consequential losses passed through as third-party claims, in exchange for a $12.5 million upfront fee. For a company with $67.3 million ARR, a single significant patent assertion against Helix’s installed base could exceed Stellarion’s total consideration under the deal.",
  "The Term Sheet language was explicit (“for the avoidance of doubt … included within”), so this is a direct reversal of a negotiated point, not a gap-fill.",
 ],
 position="Reject. Restore: indemnification obligations are subject to and included within the aggregate cap. If Helix insists on separate treatment, at most consider a separate IP indemnity super-cap no higher than the $25 million general cap, with customary exclusions and remedies (D-37)."),

As drafted, Helix’s unpaid fees and royalties could also count toward the cap."],
 position="Restore $25,000,000 and provide that Helix’s payment obligations (upfront fee, royalties, minimum royalty) are neither limited by nor counted toward the cap."),

dict(id="D-37", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Indemnity scope broadened (“infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates”; “arising out of or relating to”; successors and assigns) without customary IP indemnity exclusions or remedies",
 ref="TS §10 / EL §9.1",
 ts="Indemnity for third-party claims “arising from alleged infringement of intellectual property rights by the indemnifying party’s Background IP”; procedures to be set out in the Definitive Agreement; subject to the cap.",
 el="Indemnity for Losses “arising out of or relating to any claim that the Indemnifying Party’s Background IP, as contributed to or utilized in the arrangement … infringes, misappropriates, or otherwise violates” third-party IP; Indemnified Parties include successors and assigns. No exclusions; no mitigation remedies.",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Adding misappropriation and “otherwise violates” broadens Stellarion’s exposure beyond infringement, and “as … utilized in the arrangement” extends cover to EdgeAI as integrated, modified and combined by Helix. The letter omits standard licensor protections: no indemnity for claims caused by (a) Helix modifications (Helix has a modification right under EL §4.1), (b) combination with Helix Edge Runtime or other non-Stellarion technology, (c) use outside the Licensed Field or in breach, or (d) continued use after Stellarion supplies a non-infringing update; and no right for Stellarion to procure a license, modify or replace, or terminate and refund as its remedy. Coverage of “successors and assigns” matters given the free M&A assignment right (D-54)."],
 position="Limit to infringement or misappropriation by EdgeAI as delivered by Stellarion and used in accordance with the Agreement; add customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/terminate remedies; keep within the cap (D-35)."),

dict(id="D-39", area="G. Indemnification and Limitation of Liability",
 title="Consequential damages waiver expressly covers lost profits and revenue, with no carve-out for license scope, field-of-use, non-compete, sublicensing or payment breaches",
 ref="TS §11 / EL §9.2 (second paragraph)",
 ts="Mutual waiver of indirect, incidental, consequential, special or punitive damages. Cap exclusions: confidentiality; willful misconduct or fraud.",
 el="Waiver adds “exemplary” damages and expressly “loss of profits, loss of revenue, loss of data, loss of business opportunity, or loss of goodwill”; excepted only for the cap carve-outs (indemnity, confidentiality, willful misconduct or fraud).",
 sev="Material", favors="Helix", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=["Stellarion’s principal damages if Helix deploys EdgeAI in supply chain optimization, breaches the non-compete or sublicenses without consent would be lost profits in its core market. Expressly waiving lost profits and lost business opportunity would bar most of that recovery, leaving injunctive relief, which the exclusive arbitration clause itself makes uncertain (D-53). The Term Sheet waiver had the same basic architecture, so part of this is a gap common to both documents, but the express listing of lost profits makes the Engagement Letter materially worse."],
 position="Carve out from both the cap and the waiver: (i) use of EdgeAI or Joint IP outside the scope of the license (including the Excluded Field); (ii) breach of the non-compete and sublicensing restrictions; (iii) infringement or misappropriation of the other party’s IP; (iv) payment obligations."),

dict(id="D-40", area="H. Confidentiality",

 el="Information “designated as confidential or that … reasonably should be understood to be confidential”; prior-knowledge exception without written records; public-domain exception “through no fault”; disclosure also to “officers, … consultants, and contractors” bound by written obligations; compelled disclosure exception added; agreement terms expressly confidential.",

dict(id="D-43", area="I. Termination",
 title="Breach termination: 30-day notice running concurrently with a 30-day cure (about 30 days) instead of 60-day notice plus 30-day cure (90 days); double materiality qualifier",
 ref="TS §12.1 / EL §11.1",
 ts="60 days’ written notice; 30-day cure period; termination effective at the end of the cure period, “i.e., ninety (90) days total from delivery of the initial notice of breach.”",
 el="Termination on 30 days’ prior written notice for “a material breach … of any material provision,” if uncured 30 days after receipt of notice.",
 sev="Moderate", favors="Mixed", action="Negotiate",
 analysis=[
  "The timeline compresses from about 90 days to about 30. Because the right is mutual, it cuts both ways: Stellarion could terminate faster for Helix breaches (non-payment, field-of-use violations), but Helix could also terminate quickly (for example over a Meridian dispute) shortly after Stellarion has deposited source code and committed development resources. The double qualifier (“material breach” of a “material provision”) raises the bar to terminate and is generally unhelpful to a licensor.",
  "Term Sheet drafting note: TS §12.1 is internally inconsistent. A 30-day cure running “following receipt of such notice” expires on day 30, not day 90; the parenthetical shows the intended reading (60-day notice period followed by a 30-day cure). The Definitive Agreement should state the mechanics unambiguously.",
 ],
 position="Split regime: (i) payment defaults: 15 to 30 day cure, then termination; (ii) breaches of the field-of-use, sublicensing, confidentiality or non-compete provisions: 30 days if curable, immediate if not curable or willful; (iii) other material breaches: the Term Sheet 90-day framework. Delete “of any material provision.”"),

dict(id="D-48", area="J. Source Code Escrow",
